## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Khuddakavatthukkhandhaka* ("The chapter on minor topics" or "Minor matters") is the fifteenth chapter of the Vinaya *Khandhaka* and forms the fifth section of the *Cullavagga* [Norman 1983; Frauwallner 1956; Hazra 1994]. The chapter gathers a wide and heterogeneous set of minor rules governing monastic daily life, including regulations concerning allowable buildings and recurring prohibitions against luxurious items and sensual indulgence. Key narratives and procedures detailed in the text include the *Khandhaparitta* verses recited for protection against dangerous snakes and insects, the formal act of "overturning the bowl" (*pattanikkujjana*) enacted against laypeople who act harmfully toward the Saṅgha, and the widely discussed injunction for monastics to learn the teachings in the Buddha's own way of expression. It also treats everyday behavioral standards, such as prohibitions against the group of six monks (*chabbaggiya* / *ṣaḍvargika*) committing excesses in rubbing and anointing their bodies while bathing [Banerjee 1979]. An English translation is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Computational analysis via DharmaNexus confirms prominent cross-language alignment with the Tibetan *Vinayakṣudrakavastu* (D0006) and the Sanskrit *Poṣadhavastu* and *Carmavastu* [DharmaNexus]. Internally within the Pali canon, DharmaNexus identifies substantial textual reuse between this chapter and adjacent Khandhaka texts—particularly the *Bhikkhunikkhandhaka* (Kd 20), *Senāsanakkhandhaka* (Kd 16), *Bhesajjakkhandhaka* (Kd 6), and *Uposathakkhandhaka* (Kd 2)—as well as Vinaya commentaries such as the *Vinayālaṅkāra-ṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
